label: CONCRETE_IN_A2C_2: capable of causing: A2c defines concrete as something that can cause something
term: concrete in A2c: capable of causing
definition: A2c defines concrete as something that can cause something. This is narrower than A2P1 cause-or-effect capability. An uncaused actual individual does not acquire outgoing causal capability merely from being a graph source. The survey nominal necessary-being definition separately requires possible causal exercise and inability not to exist.
note: Pinned A2c concrete term@title. No identification with the intervention-response capacity, materiality, or all existing candidates is asserted. OPEN declaration-completion blocker (2026-11-09): capability may mean accessible-world causal exercise, an unexercised disposition, or their explicit interpretation fork. A primitive CanCause relation with an existential outgoing wrapper does not complete this original meaning. Existing TruthCore.Modal.ExistenceDegrees.PossibleCauseAt m v x y means an edge at some accessible u for the SAME rigid x and y, with no endpoint existence guards built in; choosing it here needs owner selection and explicit existence guards (at standpoint and/or witness world), quantifier scope and individual identity policy. PowerExistenceBoundary.Profile.intrinsicPower explicitly does not represent merely unexercised capacity, so is not a replacement. Do not identify sourcehood, actual exercise or materiality with capability.
